definition: First flagellomere, the first long segment of the antenna after scape and pedicel. Older keys number antennal segments from the scape, so 'antenna 3' = f1, 'antenna 4' = f2, 'antenna 5' = f3. Lengths and ratios to the labrum are used in many couplets.

definition: The 14 segments of the antennal flagellum after the scape and pedicel, numbered fI–fXIV (older keys count from the scape: antennal segments 3–16, AIII–AXVI). Galati et al. 2017 recommend recording the lengths of fI, fII, fIII and fXII–fXIV, the position of the internal and external ascoids on fI, the ascoidal formula, and the number and position of papillae and simple setae.

Hyaline sensory rod on the flagellomeres. Number per segment (antennal formula), length relative to the segment (e.g. asc/f2) and presence of spurs are diagnostic (e.g. S. gemmea and S. raynali have spurred ascoids).

Small sensilla on the flagellomeres. Galati et al. 2017 name them by position: apical (ap), preapical (pap), median (mp), basal (bp), preascoidal (pasp) and spiniform papillae (sp) (Fig. 4); their number and position on each flagellomere are recorded in descriptions. A papilla on antenna 5 (fIII) separates P. argentipes from P. philippinensis in Lewis 1978.

definition: The palp has five segments (p1–p5). The palpal formula lists them in order of increasing length, e.g. 1-2-4-3-5. Galati et al. 2017 recommend recording the lengths of p1–p5, the palpal formula, the presence and position of Newstead's sensilla on p2 and p3, and the number of spiniform setae on p3 and p4.
The dorsal mouthpart. Its length is the standard against which antenna 3 and wing length are compared.
The chamber behind the mouthparts. Its armature (teeth, sclerotized area, arch) is the most-used character in female Sergentomyia keys.

Basal segment of the male clasper. Its basal process or tuft of hairs (brush) is diagnostic.
Distal segment of the clasper. Number and position of its spines (terminal, subterminal, near middle) are used at genus and subgenus level; Sergentomyia has an accessory seta.

The sclerotized sheath through which the genital filaments emerge (older keys call it the aedeagus). Its tip shape is used in Parrotomyia and Larroussius.

Paired rods next to the sperm pump; characteristic of Idiophlebotomus.

The anepimeron (anp) is a sclerite on the side of the thorax, behind the upper and lower anepisternum (Galati et al. 2017, Fig. 10). It may bear anepimeral setae (anps, Fig. 11), whose presence or absence is recorded in descriptions. In Grassomyia the anepimeron bears scales (or their sockets), which are counted in the Lewis 1987 Grassomyia key.

Small trumpet-shaped glandular structures on the abdominal tergites of males of Chinius: 40-50 on the antero-dorsal parts of tergites 4 and 5 in Ch. barbazani, also present in Ch. junlianensis; Depaquit et al. (2006) include them in the definition of the genus.
